items.title: PJ Harvey - To Bring You My Love (1995)
items.creator: PJ Harvey
items.description: To Bring You My Love is the third studio album by PJ Harvey, released on February 27, 1995, through Island Records. Marking a bold reinvention after the raw minimalism of her earlier work, the album expands her sound with haunting blues influences, lush arrangements, and a dark, cinematic atmosphere. Featuring iconic songs such as “Down by the Water,” “C’mon Billy,” “To Bring You My Love,” and “Long Snake Moan,” the record explores themes of desire, loss, and spiritual yearning. Widely acclaimed upon release, it established PJ Harvey as one of the most distinctive and powerful voices of the 1990s. This upload is for archival and educational purposes only.

spares.title: Rave Un2 the Joy Fantastic
spares.creator: Prince
spares.description: Clive Davis convinced Prince to record a star-studded comeback album for Arista in 1999 -- much like how he coaxed Prince's idol Carlos Santana to revive his career with Supernatural. Problem is, Prince isn't willing to fully throw himself into the contemporary mainstream, as Santana did. Instead, he sticks to his guns with Rave Un2 the Joy Fantastic, delivering an album that's frighteningly similar to the lackluster New Power Soul, only a little slicker and better, and with cameos. Rave, like its predecessor, is stilted and canned, clearly the work of one man with guitars, synths, and a drum machine. It's shocking to hear how perfunctory most of the performances are on Rave, yet it's stranger to hear Prince gunning for the pop charts. items.title: Hooked On Dialectics
items.creator: Charles Ray Experience, Charles Ray Experience
items.description: The Charles Ray Experience were a legendary experimental song-based noise collage band that emerged from UCLA’s graduate art school in the early 1990s. Their line up included Hector G Romero , Doug Harvey , Colin Cook, and assorted guest performers who all performed on a variety of instruments that usually included rhythm and electric guitars, trumpets, drums, drum machines, turntables, and electronics. The original CRE material was self-recorded and self-released on cassette but now comes to you as a free download, courtesy of WFMU's Free Music Archive. If you like Lo-Fi "weird artsy rock" you will love Hooked On Dialectics. If you hate weird artsy rock, The Charles Ray Experience will torture you until you love it.
